summary.text:
Doncaster's 2026/27–2029/30 strategy commits the Council to short-term borrowing only until PWLB rates fall to an assumed neutral level of 3.5% (paragraph 60), at which point long-term drawdown resumes (paragraph 37). Their own advisor's forecast in Appendix D (MUFG, 22 December 2025) does not show any PWLB tenure certainty rate reaching 3.5% at any point in the horizon — the 5-year certainty bottoms at 3.90% in Mar-27 and stays there, 10-year at 4.50%, 25-year at 5.00%, 50-year at 4.80%. The condition on which the strategy pivots is attached to a level that MUFG themselves do not forecast.

The internal-borrowing runway shortens sharply. Under-borrowing falls from £107.9m at 31/03/25 to £30.3m at 31/03/30 on the paper's own numbers while total external debt grows by £346m over the same period. Reserves go negative from 2027/28 (-£5.6m), the driver being the DSG deficit; treatment awaits the final local government settlement 2026/27. £133.94m of fixed borrowing (29.07%) is already inside 12 months and the upper limit is being raised from 30% to 35% to accommodate more short-term rolling.

Every table foots. The balance-sheet identity CFR − OLTL − external = internal ties to the pound in every year (a 1k rounding in 2027/28). Our current PWLB file holds 44 loans with a balance around £338m at a weighted rate of about 4.4%; the paper does not split PWLB from LA temporary or market debt so a like-for-like reconciliation isn't available, but our total sits comfortably inside their £460.78m fixed at 31/12/25.

Contacts published — Clare Rosser (Assistant Directorate Finance Manager) and Matthew Smith (Head of Financial Management), both with direct dial and email at the foot of the report. Faye Tyas is named as S151 Officer without an email.

officer.body:
Hi Matthew,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep the data and the training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are a few thoughts on the 2026/27–2029/30 TMSS that went to Cabinet on 11 February after OSMC scrutiny on the 5th. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it.

A cross-check first. The balance-sheet identity in your paragraph 47 table foots every year: CFR less other long-term liabilities less external borrowing equals the printed under-borrowed number to the pound (a single £1k rounding in 2027/28). Fixed maturity buckets in Appendix A sum to £460.78m and to 100.00% exactly. Our PWLB file for you holds 44 loans with a balance around £338m at about 4.4% weighted, which sits inside your £460.78m of fixed debt at 31/12/25 — the paper doesn't split PWLB from LA temporary and market debt so a line-by-line tie isn't available, but the totals are consistent.

The reason we wrote is one line in paragraph 60. The strategy is conditional on PWLB certainty rates falling to your advisor's assumed neutral of 3.5%, at which point paragraph 37 has you resuming long-term PWLB drawdown. It's the pivot the whole approach rests on. What struck us reading Appendix D is that MUFG's own forecast doesn't reach it. Their 22 December view has the 5-year PWLB standard rate bottoming at 4.10% in March 2027 and staying there — 3.90% on certainty. The 10-year bottoms at 4.60% (4.40% certainty), 25-year at 5.20%, 50-year at 5.00%. The condition on which the strategy turns is attached to a level MUFG themselves do not forecast at any tenure, at any point in the horizon.

On this afternoon's PWLB fixing, notice 314/26, the 5-year certainty rate is 5.34%, the 10-year 5.83%, the 25-year 6.46%. Roughly 100 basis points above where MUFG had the 5-year eight months ago, and above their end-of-2028 numbers. We publish this at both fixings alongside the monthly breakdown of every loan the sector actually drew — July was £368m across 33 loans from 19 borrowers at an average 5.02%, which is thin, and thin PWLB months are when the LA-to-LA market gets expensive too. It sits at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity.

Why that matters for Doncaster specifically is the internal-borrowing runway. Paragraph 44 has reserves going negative from 2027/28, driver the DSG deficit, and the under-borrowed line in paragraph 47 falls from £107.9m at 31 March 2025 to £30.3m by 31 March 2030 while total external debt grows by £346m. £133.94m of the fixed book is already inside 12 months, the upper limit is being raised from 30% to 35% for 2026/27, and the £57m Airport City borrowing from paragraphs 38–39 is still to land in next year's TMSS. The 3.5% precondition is doing a lot of work in that picture.

On pricing: the book is about £59.7m below par on the DMO's premature repayment curve today, 32 of 44 loans in discount, largest discounts on the low-rate long-dated HRA-era loans. Standard caveats and we mean them — we don't sell treasury products, we model no MRP or accounting treatment, and only the DMO can quote. Yours is at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis. Your paragraph 70 already notes surplus cash for any repayment is unlikely; the number is there if the position changes.

On training, four fit Doncaster. Strategic PWLB borrowing sits directly against the paragraph 37 pivot. Intra-LA borrowing & lending markets because that is where the short-term book is going. Liability benchmark & internal borrowing because the runway is measurable and worth putting in front of members. And PWLB break costs — mechanics & live calculator. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew
